_comment: Branch protection for `develop` — US-01.1.1 T-01.1.1.3. Applied by scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh, asserted by scripts/verify-branch-protection.sh. Do not edit on GitHub directly; edit here and re-apply so the configuration stays reviewable and restorable.
_strict_note: required_status_checks.strict = true enforces 'branch must be up to date before merging' (AC-2). DEV-02 is closed: the contexts below are the full pipeline (US-01.4.1) and are now actually required, not merely described.
_contexts_note: Every context here must report on EVERY pull request, or protection waits forever for a check that never arrives and the branch becomes unmergeable. That is why frontend.yml dropped its pull-request path filter — its two jobs are required, and a path-filtered workflow does not run at all for an unrelated PR. Names are the job `name:` values as GitHub reports them.
_codeql_note: `sast-codeql` (our workflow job, which runs the analysis) is required; the separate `CodeQL` check published by the github-advanced-security app is deliberately NOT. It comes from a different app whose availability is not ours to guarantee, and a required check that stops being published deadlocks every pull request. The analysis itself is already gated by sast-codeql.
_enforce_admins_note: AC-4 — administrators cannot push directly to develop.
_reviews_note: DEVIATION from AC-2/AC-3: required_approving_review_count is 0 and require_code_owner_reviews is false. GitHub never requests review from a PR author, and this repository has one owner, so any non-zero requirement would block every merge permanently. Raise to 1 (2 for ACS/security paths) and enable code-owner review the moment a second collaborator or an organisation exists. See docs/project/13-branch-protection.md.
_linear_note: develop takes squash merges from feature branches, so history is linear by construction. main differs — see main.json.
